name: Family Reunification (Reagrupación Familiar)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires the sponsor to hold at least 1 year of legal residence, renewed or authorized for at least another year.
requirements.fix_path: Wait until the sponsor reaches the required residence tenure.

requirements.blocker_text: This covers spouse/registered partner (not separated), minor children (of the sponsor or spouse), dependent adult children with a disability, and ascendants over 65 (only if the sponsor holds long-term residence).

value.note: for sponsor + 1 reunited family member; +50% IPREM per additional member

requirements.blocker_text: This requires the sponsor to show income of at least €900/month (150% of IPREM) for reuniting with 1 family member, plus €300/month (50% of IPREM) for each additional member.
requirements.fix_path: Increase income to the required level.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires an informe de habitabilidad/adecuación de vivienda (housing adequacy report) from the local town hall or autonomous community.

evidence_required.document: Marriage/partnership certificate or birth certificate proving family tie
Housing adequacy report from the local authority

sources.title: BOE — Real Decreto 1155/2024 (Reglamento de Extranjería), Arts. 65-68

notes: FORMULA VALUE, tier-1 confirmed as pegged to IPREM at exactly 150% (2 members) + 50% per additional member. STALE-DATA FLAG: some tier-3 sites publish €940/month for the base 2-member figure, inconsistent with the frozen €600 IPREM (150% of €600 is exactly €900, not €940) — likely a computational error or reliance on an outdated IPREM value on the source's end. A REDUCED threshold (tied to the Ingreso Mínimo Vital/renta garantizada, approximately €724/month for 2 members) can apply when the reunited family member is a minor — not modeled as a separate requirement group here, flagged as a real simplification pending further detail. Timeline structure is genuinely multi-stage and worth surfacing distinctly: administration resolves within 2 months, the family member then has 2 months to apply for the visa at the consulate, and 3 months to actually enter Spain — three separate clocks, not one, a level of process detail not present on most other countries' family routes in this dataset.
